articles.title: Fantastic Fleetwood seal shootout success in Carabao Cup shock against Arsenal
articles.summary: It’s more than 20 years since Arsenal played at Highbury but their trip to League Two Fleetwood – and a stadium of the same name – did not bring back fond memories as they were dumped out of the Carabao Cup on penalties.
body: Aaron Loupalo-Bi and Viktor Gyökeres exchanged goals in normal time but Arsenal were unable to find a winner, despite being the dominant force, as Fleetwood battled to the end. Goalkeeper Jay Lynch held his nerve to save from Bruno Guimarães in the shootout before the teenager Conor Haughey scored the winner and created a delirious pitch invasion.

Fleetwood wanted to make the occasion into a party as pyrotechnics galore were set off before the match, sending an acrid red mist across the pitch. Once the whistle went, however, the fun quickly stopped as a drone flying above the pitch forced the referee Michael Salisbury to pause play.

The two teams had to stay warm in the chilly conditions, passing balls around while officials tried to rectify the situation. Fleetwood staff looked angry that their moment in the limelight was being blighted by this. After six minutes, officials called the players to the touchline and spoke to both head coaches, before restarting play after a chat with a member of the local constabulary, concluding the chant of “Who’s the wanker with the drone?”. All good knockabout stuff.

articles.title: Glens secure Challenge Cup with Reds shootout win
articles.summary: Kelly Bailie scores the winning penalty for Glentoran in her final match to secure the Challenge Cup with a shootout win over Cliftonville at Windsor Park.
body: Bailie, 46, netted the final spot-kick in the shootout in her last game for the east Belfast club after 30 years.

The final had plenty of talking points in the build-up with Brendan Lynch's side being stripped of their League Cup title after they fielded two ineligible players against the Glens and the showpiece being delayed by three days due to Storm Boelo.
However, the final itself did not produce many memorable moments before the penalty shootout which the Glens won 4-2.
Cliftonville started the season finale on the front foot with Kirsty McGuinness' deflected shot, which had wrong-footed stopper Ellie Scott, going narrowly wide.

articles.title: An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur
articles.summary: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows. Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape.
body: Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure. Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door.

Beyond Busby and Ferguson, each United manager who also served felt the lash of desperation of a falling giant. Each of their defenestrations has featured an infighting that would not have been out of place in ancient Rome. Favouritism, nepotism, self-interest, entitlement, complacency and sentimentality have been the betrayal of a legend, to use the title of Michael Crick’s and David Smith’s “ j’accuse ” book from 1989. Living with the legend and influence of those two managers leads the list of difficulties.
points: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows.
Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United.

articles.title: Sliding Colts trade All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson to Seahawks for draft picks
articles.summary: 30-year-old is an eight-time Pro Bowl selection. Indianapolis fired GM Ballard last week amid skid. The Indianapolis Colts have traded All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks, a person with knowledge of the deal told the Associated Press on Tuesday.
body: The person requested anonymity because the deal had not been announced by either team and said the Colts would receive a third-round draft pick and a fifth-round pick in return for the eight-time Pro Bowler.
Nelson can become a free agent in March, but he had not said much about his future plans because he was focused on finishing this season strong.

It’s the second major move in two weeks for Indianapolis (2-5), who have lost three straight and 12 of their past 14 overall. The Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard last week after a loss to the previously winless Tennessee Titans at home. Assistant general manager Ed Dodds has replaced Ballard for now.

Nelson was the No 6 overall pick in 2018 and joined linebacker Darius Leonard on the All-Pro team, making the duo the first rookie teammates to earn All-Pro honors since the Chicago Bears’ Gale Sayers and Dick Butkus in 1965. Nelson was an All-Pro from 2018 to 2020.

articles.title: Arsenal dumped out of Carabao Cup by League Two Fleetwood
articles.summary: Fleetwood Town produced one of the biggest shocks in Carabao Cup history as the League Two team dumped out Premier League champions Arsenal on penalties to reach the quarter-finals.
body: Mikel Arteta named a strong Arsenal side with Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz up front and Martin Odegaard playing the second half.
But they were not at the races, as the team two points above the League Two relegation zone took them to a 1-1 draw after Max Dowman was sent off before the shoot-out.
Then Bruno Guimaraes saw his penalty saved by Fleetwood goalkeeper Jay Lynch - who also made wonder saves to deny Ben White and Odegaard in stoppage time.
That left Conor Haughey to blast past Illan Meslier - picked by Arteta over penalty expert Kepa Arrizabalaga to make his Arsenal debut - to send Highbury mad.

articles.title: Yarde still targeting long-awaited showdown with Buatsi
articles.summary: Anthony Yarde is still targeting a fight with domestic rival Joshua Buatsi if he wins his clash with Willy Hutchinson for the vacant WBC light heavyweight world title.
body: Two years on from their first fight back in 2024, Buatsi takes on Hutchinson on November 7 at the AO Arena in Manchester.
Buatsi emerged victorious in their first meeting after dropping Hutchinson twice then winning via decision.
Now, Yarde is backing Buatsi to claim the win because that means they are one step closer to finally meeting in the ring.

Yarde has long been linked with a fight against his fellow light-heavyweight, with the two men seemingly on a collision course ever since Buatsi turned professional after winning bronze at the 2016 Olympics in Rio de Janeiro.

articles.title: Fleetwood-Arsenal halted for eight minutes because of drone
articles.summary: Arsenal's match with Fleetwood Town in the last-16 of the Carabao Cup is delayed for more than eight minutes after a drone is spotted above the stadium during the match.
body: Arsenal's match against Fleetwood Town in the last-16 of the Carabao Cup was delayed for more than eight minutes after a drone was flown above the stadium while play was ongoing.
Referee Michael Salisbury stopped proceedings with one minute and 40 seconds on the clock after spotting the drone flying above the pitch while Arsenal waited to take a free-kick at Highbury Stadium.
The game was halted while the referee spoke to the management and staff on both benches, with police also investigating.
The match got back under way with 10 minutes on the clock. A commentator for Sky later said police had located the drone operator.

articles.title: Ballon d'Or in London - the most chaotic ever?
articles.summary: It was the first time the Ballon d'Or had been held in London in its 70-year history - but the event was not plain sailing. BBC Sport assesses a chaotic night.
body: Despite the perfect homecoming for Harry Kane on Monday night, the rest of the event was not plain sailing.
Did the organisers give away the winners early or was it just a simple mix-up? Why was the ceremony delayed and why was the audience booing?

London traffic can cause issues on any day but unfortunately for the Ballon d'Or organisers, they chose to hold a major event just a stone's throw from Oxford Street on the same day the famous shopping area was made traffic-free.
That, coupled with large crowds at the event entrance, meant significant numbers of guests were delayed and the start had to be pushed back by 45 minutes.

articles.title: Cagliari joy as Trepy returns 2 months after nearly drowning
articles.summary: Cagliari may have lost 4-2 to Roma, but the most important success story of the night was the return to the field of Yael Trepy, two months after he nearly died in a swimming pool.
body: The 20-year-old striker had impressed for the Sardinians in pre-season and started their Coppa Italia win over Arezzo on August 14.
It was three days after that he was enjoying some time off in a rented villa with friends when he took a dip in the swimming pool, not realising how deep it was, and got into difficulty.
He was rushed to hospital and kept in intensive care while the fluid was removed from his lungs, making a full recovery.
That process was completed today when Trepy came off the bench in Cagliari’s 4-2 Serie A defeat to Roma at the Stadio Olimpico.

articles.title: Eyeing Future World Cup Success, U.S. Soccer Uplifting Young Stars For LA Olympics
articles.summary: On the way to the FIFA 2030 World Cup, U.S. men's soccer prospects Cavan Sullivan and Julian Hall could be key members of the 2028 Olympic hosts' squad in Los Angeles.
body: When a new generation of blue-chip teenagers recently led the U.S. men’s soccer team to four convincing wins in its first four games since capturing the imagination of the American public during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, optimism about the program's future surged among USA fans old and new.
Perhaps nobody was happier about how Cavan Sullivan, Julian Hall and the rest of the youngsters fared than U.S. Soccer COO Dan Helfrich.

In less than a year in the role, the former Deloitte executive has quietly emerged as one of the most influential figures in the domestic game. Helfrich, who has overseen the federation’s day-to-day operations since January, and CEO JT Batson made the decision to sign coach Mauricio Pochettino to a new four-year contract following the Stars and Stripes' stirring run to the World Cup round of 16.

And it was Helfrich who spearheaded the successful recruitment of three-time former U.S. World Cup defender Steve Cherundolo, an MLS Cup-winning coach with LAFC in 2022, to lead the American men at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles.
